## Setup and Summary Statistics

```{r setup-and-summary-statistics}
rm(list=ls()) #remove any data objects or functions to avoid collisions or misspecification

#BiocManager::install("snpStats",force=TRUE) #run only once to install
#BiocManager::install("SNPRelate",force=TRUE) #run only once to install

library(snpStats)
library(SNPRelate)
library(gdsfmt)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Consistent look for all ggplot2 figures: minimal theme, light blue for single-variable plots, red for thresholds
theme_set(theme_minimal())
lightBlue <- "lightblue"
darkBlue <- "#08519C"
thresholdColour <- "firebrick"

# Naturally, adapt this to your own compute environment
getwd()
# Load Lab 1 results from the current project directory.
load("lab1_save.RData")

# Keep track of how many individuals and SNPs remain after each QC step
qcSteps <- data.frame(step = "Start", individuals = nrow(genotype), SNPs = ncol(genotype))

#specificy the number of threads for IBD and PCA functions
numCores=4

# calculate summary statistics for the genotype matrix per variant (column)
# and per individual (row)
snpsum.row <- row.summary(genotype) #from snpStats
snpsum.col<-col.summary(genotype)
```

## Call Rate

```{r call-rate}
# To filter by call rate, we remove individuals that are missing genotype data across
# more than a pre-defined percentage of the typed SNPs. This proportion of missingness
# across SNPs is the sample call rate and we apply a threshold of 95%, meaning that we
# drop those individuals missing genotype data for more than 5% of the typed SNPs. A
# new reduced dimesion SnpMatrix gentotype is created from this filter.

samplecall.thresh <- 0.95

# Subset the genotype and clinical data to remove the individuals that do not pass the criteria
keep.samplecall <- with(snpsum.row, !is.na(Call.rate) & Call.rate > samplecall.thresh)
keep.samplecall[is.na(keep.samplecall)] <- FALSE

ggplot(snpsum.row, aes(x = Call.rate)) +
  geom_histogram(fill = lightBlue, colour = "white", bins = 50, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = samplecall.thresh, colour = thresholdColour, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Sample call rate before filtering",
       subtitle = paste(nrow(genotype) - sum(keep.samplecall), "individuals below the threshold"),
       x = "Sample call rate", y = "Number of individuals")

cat(nrow(genotype)-sum(keep.samplecall), "individuals will be removed due to low sample call rate.\n")

genotype <- genotype[keep.samplecall,]
clinical<- clinical[ rownames(genotype), ]
snpsum.row<-row.summary(genotype)
qcSteps <- rbind(qcSteps, data.frame(step = "Sample call rate", individuals = nrow(genotype), SNPs = ncol(genotype)))
```

## Heterozygosity

```{r heterozygosity}
# Heterozygosity refers to the presence of each of two alleles at a given SNP
# within an individual. This is expected under Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium (HWE)
# to occur with probability of 2p(1-p) where p is the dominant allele frequency
# at that SNP (assuming a bi-allelic SNP). Excess or deficient heterozygosity
# across typed SNPs within an individual is commonly considered as an indication
# of inbreeding but also serves as a screen for poor sample quality.


# In this lab, heterozygosity F statistic calculation is carried out with the form,
# |F|=(1-O/E), where O is observed proportion of heterozygous genotypes for a given
# sample and E is the expected proportion of heterozygous genotypes for a given
# sample based on the minor allele frequency across all non-missing SNPs for a given
# sample. We will remove any sample with inbreeding coefficient |F| > 0.05, which
# might indicate autozygosity (which is not inherently a problem, but perhaps
# unusual) or poor quality sample.

# What type of poor quality sample is heterozygosity based quality control
# likely to identify?

# Recalculate the allele frequencies and the call matrix for the individuals that remain
snpsum.col<-col.summary(genotype)
MAF <- snpsum.col$MAF
callmatrix <- !is.na(genotype)

hetExp <- callmatrix %*% (2*MAF*(1-MAF)) #Note that %*% is base R matrix multiplication
hetObs <- with(snpsum.row, Heterozygosity*(ncol(genotype))*Call.rate)
snpsum.row$hetF <- 1-(hetObs/hetExp)

head(snpsum.row)

het.thresh <- 0.05

keep.het <- with(snpsum.row, abs(hetF) <= het.thresh)
keep.het[is.na(keep.het)] <- FALSE

ggplot(data.frame(hetF = as.numeric(snpsum.row$hetF)), aes(x = hetF)) +
  geom_histogram(fill = lightBlue, colour = "white", bins = 50, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-het.thresh, het.thresh), colour = thresholdColour, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Heterozygosity F statistic across individuals",
       subtitle = paste(nrow(genotype) - sum(keep.het), "individuals outside the threshold"),
       x = "Heterozygosity F statistic", y = "Number of individuals")

ggplot(data.frame(hetObs = as.numeric(hetObs), hetExp = as.numeric(hetExp), keep = keep.het),
       aes(x = hetExp, y = hetObs, colour = keep)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("TRUE" = lightBlue, "FALSE" = thresholdColour),
                      labels = c("TRUE" = "Retained", "FALSE" = "Removed")) +
  labs(title = "Observed vs. expected heterozygous genotypes per individual",
       x = "Expected number of heterozygous genotypes", y = "Observed number of heterozygous genotypes", colour = "")
cat(nrow(genotype)-sum(keep.het), "individuals will be removed due to unusual F coefficient.\n")
```

```{r subset-after-heterozygosity}
# As before, after identifying the individuals to be removed, we subset the genotype
# and clinical data set using information obtained above to remove the individuals
# that do not pass the criteria from our sample.

genotype <- genotype[keep.het,]
clinical<- clinical[rownames(genotype), ]
# After removing individuals, summary statistics of the genetic data change.
# Recalculate sumstats
snpsum.row<-row.summary(genotype)
qcSteps <- rbind(qcSteps, data.frame(step = "Heterozygosity", individuals = nrow(genotype), SNPs = ncol(genotype)))
```

## Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium

```{r hardy-weinberg-equilibrium}
# Why calculate HWE based only on the CAD controls?
# How many variants are omitted comparing controls only vs. the whole sample?

hardy.thresh <- 10^-6     #the threshold is parameterized as a p-value, not a z score as in col.summary
# Serum urate is a quantitative trait.
# No validated CAD control group is available.
# Calculate HWE using all individuals retained after sample QC.
controls <- rownames(genotype)
stopifnot(length(controls) == nrow(genotype))
# use col.summary on genetic data from controls only
snpsum.colControls <- col.summary(genotype[controls,])
#use qnorm to convert the p value threshold 'hardy' to a z score
keep.hwe <- with(snpsum.colControls, !is.na(z.HWE) & ( abs(z.HWE) < abs( qnorm(hardy.thresh/2) ) ) )

ggplot(data.frame(absZ = abs(snpsum.colControls$z.HWE)), aes(x = absZ)) +
  geom_histogram(fill = lightBlue, colour = "white", bins = 50, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = abs(qnorm(hardy.thresh/2)), colour = thresholdColour, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_sqrt() +
  labs(title = "Hardy-Weinberg deviation in retained samples",
       subtitle = paste(sum(is.na(keep.hwe) | !keep.hwe), "SNPs beyond the threshold"),
       x = "Absolute HWE z score", y = "Number of SNPs (square root scale)")

# We can delete this object now
rm(snpsum.colControls)

keep.hwe[is.na(keep.hwe)] <- FALSE

cat(ncol(genotype)-sum(keep.hwe),"SNPs will be removed due to deviation from HWE.\n")

# Subset the genotype data yet again
genotype <- genotype[,keep.hwe]
genoMap <- genoMap[colnames(genotype), , drop = FALSE]
stopifnot(identical(colnames(genotype), rownames(genoMap)))
qcSteps <- rbind(qcSteps, data.frame(step = "HWE", individuals = nrow(genotype), SNPs = ncol(genotype)))

# Check the dimensionality of the working genotype matrix
print(genotype)
```

## Cryptic Relatedness, Duplicates and Gender Identity

```{r cryptic-relatedness}
# Population-based cohort studies often only concerns unrelated individuals and
# the generalized linear modeling approach assumes independence across individuals.
# In regional cohort studies (e.g. hospital-based cohort studies) of complex
# diseases, however, individuals from the same family could be unintentionally
# recruited. To mitigate this problem, we thus employ Identity-by-descent (IBD)
# analysis which is a common measurement of relateness and duplication. Note that
# gender identity can also be checked at this stage to confirm self-reported gender
# consistency on X and Y chromosomes. With this data, we do not check gender
# identity due to unavailibility of sex chromosomes information.

# To filter on relateness criteria, we use the SNPRelate package to perform
# identity-by-descent (IBD) analysis. This package requires that the data be
# transformed into a GDS format file. IBD analysis is performed on only a subset
# of SNPs that are in linkage equilibrium by iteratively removing adjacent SNPs
# that exceed an linkage disequilibrium (LD) threshold in a sliding window using
# the snpgdsLDpruning() function. In this lab, we set LD threshold to be .2
# (max R2 between two SNPs is 0.2) and
# kinship threshold to be 6.25%, which means that we would remove SNPs in LD above
# the LD threshold from the IBD analysis, and remove one member of any pair of
# individuals whose kinship is at or above the kinship threshold. Then we used
# snpgdsBED2GDS to create a GDS file of the data set from .bim, .bed and .fam files.

ld.thresh <- 0.2   #maximum r2 between variants in 0.2
kin.thresh <- 0.0625 #for context, the kinship coefficient for 1st cousins is 0.0625
# twins is 1, unrelated near 0

# Create a specialized 'genetic data set' or .gds object using a function from
# SNPRelate package. It reads from the original files, and subsets to the individuals and
# and variants in the current 'genotype' object
snpgdsBED2GDS(bedFile, famFile, bimFile,"GWAS_data.gds")
genofile <- snpgdsOpen("GWAS_data.gds", readonly = FALSE)
gds.ids <- read.gdsn(index.gdsn(genofile, "sample.id"))
gds.ids <- sub("-1", "", gds.ids)
add.gdsn(genofile, "sample.id", gds.ids, replace = TRUE)


# Generate a subset of variants in low linkage disequilibrium for IBD and PCA,
# as these methods assume independence of variants
set.seed(1000)
snpSUB <- snpgdsLDpruning(genofile,
                          verbose=TRUE,
                          ld.threshold = ld.thresh,
                          maf=0.05,
                          missing.rate=0.05,
                          sample.id = rownames(genotype),
                          snp.id = colnames(genotype))

snpset.LoLD <- unlist(snpSUB, use.names=FALSE)


cat(length(snpset.LoLD),"will be used in IBD analysis\n")

# Use another function in SNPRelate to estimate Identity by Descent between
# all participants using a Method of Moments estimator
geno.sample.ids <- rownames(genotype)
ibd <- snpgdsIBDMoM(genofile, kinship=TRUE, sample.id = geno.sample.ids, snp.id = snpset.LoLD,  num.thread = numCores)
ibdcoeff_all <- snpgdsIBDSelection(ibd)

head(ibdcoeff_all)

#select those pairs that have kinship greater than the threshold value for
# further evaluation
kins<-subset(ibdcoeff_all,ibdcoeff_all$kinship>=kin.thresh)

```

```{r remove-related-samples}
# Greedy removal: repeatedly remove the sample involved in the most remaining related pairs
# (ties go to the sample with the lower call rate), then drop every pair that sample was in.
# This removes the fewest samples, never lists a sample twice, and is deterministic.
related.samples <- c()
pairs <- kins[, c("ID1", "ID2")]
while (nrow(pairs) > 0) {
    counts <- table(c(pairs$ID1, pairs$ID2))
    worst  <- names(counts)[counts == max(counts)]
    drop.id <- worst[which.min(snpsum.row[worst, "Call.rate"])]
    related.samples <- c(related.samples, drop.id)
    pairs <- pairs[pairs$ID1 != drop.id & pairs$ID2 != drop.id, ]
}

#Subset the genotype and clinical data yet again
genotype <- genotype[ !(rownames(genotype) %in% related.samples), ]
clinical <- clinical[ !(clinical$FamID %in% related.samples), ]

# Recompute the sample IDs so that the removed relatives are excluded from the PCA below
geno.sample.ids <- rownames(genotype)
qcSteps <- rbind(qcSteps, data.frame(step = "Relatedness", individuals = nrow(genotype), SNPs = ncol(genotype)))

cat(length(related.samples), " samples removed due to kinship >=", kin.thresh,"\n")

```

```{r ibd-plots, dev = "png"}
#evaluate the distribution of pairwise kinships
#this is ALL PAIRS of individuals, mostly minimally related (unrelated)

# Expected IBD0 and IBD1 for well-known relationships
ibdReference <- data.frame(k0 = c(1, 0.25, 0, 0), k1 = c(0, 0.5, 1, 0),
                           label = c("Unrelated", "Full siblings", "Parent-child", "Duplicate / twins"))

ggplot(ibdcoeff_all, aes(x = k0, y = k1)) +
  geom_point(colour = lightBlue, size = 0.5) +
  geom_point(data = kins, colour = thresholdColour, size = 1.5) +
  geom_point(data = ibdReference, shape = 4, size = 3) +
  geom_text(data = ibdReference, aes(label = label), vjust = -1, size = 3) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-0.05, 1.05), ylim = c(-0.05, 1.1)) +
  labs(title = "IBD of all pairs of individuals",
       subtitle = paste(nrow(kins), "pairs at or above the kinship threshold shown in red"),
       x = "IBD0", y = "IBD1")

ggplot(ibdcoeff_all, aes(x = kinship)) +
  geom_histogram(fill = lightBlue, colour = "white", bins = 60) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = kin.thresh, colour = thresholdColour, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_sqrt() +
  labs(title = "Pairwise kinship coefficients", x = "Kinship coefficient", y = "Number of pairs (square root scale)")
```

## PCA

```{r pca}
# Principle components of Ancestry is one approach to visualizing and classifying
# individuals into ancestry groups based on their observed genetic similarity.
# There are two reasons for doing this. First, self-reported ancestry can
# differ from clusters of individuals that are based on genetics infomation.
# Second, the presence of an individual not appearing to fall within a genetic
# similarity cluster may be suggestive of a sample error.

# Use another function from SNPRelate to generate PCs, by default, this function estimates
# the first 32 PCs
pca <- snpgdsPCA(genofile, sample.id = geno.sample.ids,  snp.id = snpset.LoLD, num.thread=numCores)

pcs <- data.frame(FamID = pca$sample.id, pca$eigenvect[,1 : 10], stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

colnames(pcs)[2:11]<-paste("pc", 1:10, sep = "")

print(head(pcs))

pctab <- data.frame(sample.id = pca$sample.id,
                    PC1 = pca$eigenvect[,1],
                    PC2 = pca$eigenvect[,2],
                    PC3 = pca$eigenvect[,3],
                    PC4 = pca$eigenvect[,4],
                    PC5 = pca$eigenvect[,5],
                    PC6 = pca$eigenvect[,6],
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Add case-control status and sex so that the ancestry plots can be coloured by them
sample.match <- match(pctab$sample.id, clinical$FamID)
stopifnot(!anyNA(sample.match))

pctab$Serum_Urate_mgdL <- as.numeric(
  as.character(clinical$Serum_Urate_mgdL[sample.match])
)
pctab$sex <- clinical$sex[match(pctab$sample.id, clinical$FamID)]

pcLabel <- function(i) paste0("Principal component ", i, " (", round(100*pca$varprop[i], 1), "% of variance)")

ggplot(
  pctab,
  aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, colour = Serum_Urate_mgdL)
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_colour_gradient(
    low = lightBlue,
    high = darkBlue,
    na.value = "grey70"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Genetic population structure by serum urate",
    x = pcLabel(1),
    y = pcLabel(2),
    colour = "Serum urate (mg/dL)"
  )

ggplot(pctab, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, colour = sex)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(lightBlue, darkBlue), labels = c("Male", "Female")) +
  labs(title = "Ancestry plot by sex", x = pcLabel(1), y = pcLabel(2), colour = "Sex")

# What about the other PCs? Any structure apparent there?
pcPairs <- combn(1:4, 2)
pctabPairs <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(ncol(pcPairs)), function(i) {
  data.frame(pair = paste0("PC", pcPairs[1, i], " (x) vs PC", pcPairs[2, i], " (y)"),
             x = pctab[[paste0("PC", pcPairs[1, i])]],
             y = pctab[[paste0("PC", pcPairs[2, i])]])
}))

ggplot(pctabPairs, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_point(colour = lightBlue, size = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ pair, scales = "free") +
  labs(title = "Principal components 1 to 4, pairwise", x = "Principal component (x)", y = "Principal component (y)")

# To evaluate the pattern of how much genetic variation is captured by PCs,
# we plot the percent of variance explained by each eigenvector.

ggplot(data.frame(PC = 1:20, variance = 100*pca$varprop[1:20]), aes(x = PC, y = variance)) +
  geom_col(fill = lightBlue) +
  labs(title = "Scree plot", x = "Index of eigenvector", y = "Variance explained (%)")
```

## QC Summary

```{r qc-attrition-summary}
qcSteps

qcLong <- data.frame(step = factor(rep(qcSteps$step, 2), levels = qcSteps$step),
                     what = rep(c("Individuals", "SNPs"), each = nrow(qcSteps)),
                     count = c(qcSteps$individuals, qcSteps$SNPs))

ggplot(qcLong, aes(x = step, y = count)) +
  geom_col(fill = lightBlue) +
  geom_text(aes(label = count), vjust = -0.3, size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~ what, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(title = "Individuals and SNPs remaining after each QC step", x = "QC step", y = "Number remaining") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```
